title: Pulse, Blood Pressure and Respiratory Rate — Getting Them Right Every Time

hook.en: Most wrong blood pressures are wrong because of the set-up, not the patient. Learn how to take a pulse, a blood pressure and a respiratory rate so well that a colleague gets the same numbers.
hook.ur: Zyada tar ghalat blood pressure setup ki wajah se ghalat hotay hain, patient ki wajah se nahi. Pulse, blood pressure aur respiratory rate itni achi tarah lena seekhein ke colleague ko wohi numbers milen.

goal.en: By the end, you'll take a radial pulse, a manual blood pressure and a respiratory rate correctly, know the normal adult values and spot the usual errors.
goal.ur: End tak aap radial pulse, manual blood pressure aur respiratory rate sahi lenge, normal adult values jaanenge aur aam ghaltiyan pehchanenge.

text.en: At rest in a healthy adult: **pulse 60–100 beats per minute**, **blood pressure about 120/80 mmHg** and **respiratory rate 12–20 breaths per minute**. A pulse tells you the **rate, rhythm and strength**; a blood pressure tells you how hard the heart pushes (**systolic**) and how much the vessels resist (**diastolic**); the respiratory rate is the most sensitive early sign that a patient is getting sick.
text.ur: Aaraam mein healthy adult mein: **pulse 60–100 beats per minute**, **blood pressure takriban 120/80 mmHg** aur **respiratory rate 12–20 breaths per minute**. Pulse **rate, rhythm aur strength** batati hai; blood pressure batata hai ke dil kitna zor se dhakelta hai (**systolic**) aur vessels kitni resistance dete hain (**diastolic**); respiratory rate is baat ki sab se sensitive shuruati nishani hai ke mareez bimar ho raha hai.

text.en: Blood pressure is like water in a garden hose. Systolic is the pressure when the tap is pushed open (the heart contracts); diastolic is the pressure that remains when the tap relaxes (the heart refills). Too narrow a hose (stiff arteries) or too much water (high volume) raises both numbers.
text.ur: Blood pressure bagh ki hose mein paani ki tarah hai. Systolic woh pressure hai jab tap kholi jati hai (dil contract hota hai); diastolic woh pressure hai jo tap dheeli hone par baqi rehta hai (dil bharta hai). Bohat tang hose (sakht arteries) ya bohat zyada paani (zyada volume) dono numbers ko barhata hai.

intro.en: Place **two fingertips (never your thumb)** on the radial artery at the thumb side of the wrist. Count the beats for **30 seconds and double it**, or for a full 60 seconds if the rhythm is irregular, and note the rate, rhythm and strength.
intro.ur: **Do fingertips (kabhi apna thumb nahi)** wrist ki thumb side par radial artery par rakhein. **30 seconds** ke beats ginein aur **double** karein, ya rhythm irregular ho to poore 60 seconds, aur rate, rhythm aur strength note karein.

question.en: Why should you not use your thumb to take a pulse?
question.ur: Pulse lene ke liye apna thumb kyun nahi use karte?

text.en: The thumb has its own pulse, which can be mistaken for the patient's
text.ur: Thumb ki apni pulse hoti hai jo patient ki pulse samajh li ja sakti hai

feedback.en: Yes — use the pads of the index and middle fingers.
feedback.ur: Haan — index aur middle fingers ke pads use karein.

feedback.en: Fingertips are more sensitive; the problem is the thumb's own pulse.
feedback.ur: Fingertips zyada sensitive hain; masla thumb ki apni pulse ka hai.

feedback.en: Pressure is not the main issue.

intro.en: The cuff is 2–3 cm above the elbow crease with the arm at heart level; the stethoscope sits over the brachial artery. Inflate about 30 mmHg above where the pulse disappears, deflate at **2–3 mmHg per second**: the first sound is systolic, the sounds vanishing is diastolic. Normal adult about 120/80; take two readings and average.
intro.ur: Cuff elbow crease se 2–3 cm upar, arm dil ki level par; stethoscope brachial artery ke upar. Pulse ghayab hone wali jagah se takriban 30 mmHg upar tak inflate karein, **2–3 mmHg per second** deflate karein: pehli awaz systolic hai, awaz ka ghayab hona diastolic. Normal adult takriban 120/80; do readings le kar average karein.

title.en: A good blood pressure in six steps
title.ur: Acha blood pressure chhe steps mein

steps.title: Rest and posture
steps.detail: Seated for 5 minutes, back supported, feet flat, legs uncrossed, arm supported at heart level. No talking, no recent exercise, caffeine or smoking in the last 30 minutes. || Rest aur posture

steps.title: Right cuff size
steps.detail: The bladder should cover about 80% of the arm circumference; a cuff that is too small reads falsely high. || Sahi cuff size

steps.title: Estimate the systolic first
steps.detail: Feel the radial pulse while inflating and note where it disappears; inflate 20–30 mmHg above that for the real reading. || Pehle systolic ka andaza lagayein

steps.title: Deflate slowly
steps.detail: 2–3 mmHg per second, listening over the brachial artery. Korotkoff phase I is systolic; phase V (sounds disappear) is diastolic. || Aahista deflate karein

steps.title: Repeat and record
steps.detail: Wait a minute, take a second reading, use the average and record arm, position, cuff size and any symptoms. || Dohrayein aur likhein

text.en: **Talking, a crossed leg or a cuff over clothes.** Each can add 5–10 mmHg or more. A full bladder, an unsupported arm or legs crossed also raise the reading. Another trap is deflating too fast, which under-reads the diastolic. Take both arms at the first visit; a difference above 10–15 mmHg is worth referral. And never trust a single high reading: repeat after rest, and use home or ambulatory readings to confirm hypertension.
text.ur: **Baat cheet, taang par taang ya kapron par cuff.** Har ek 5–10 mmHg ya zyada barha sakta hai. Bhara hua mesana, bina sahare ka arm ya taang par taang bhi reading barhate hain. Ek aur jaal: bohat tez deflate karna jo diastolic ko kam dikhata hai. Pehli visit par dono arms lein; 10–15 mmHg se zyada farq refer karne ke qabil hai. Aur ek akeli zyada reading par bharosa na karein: rest ke baad dohrayein aur hypertension ki tasdeeq ke liye ghar ya ambulatory readings use karein.

question.en: A patient's blood pressure is 152/94 immediately after climbing the stairs to your clinic. What should you do?
question.ur: Patient ka blood pressure seerhiyan charh kar clinic aane ke foran baad 152/94 hai. Kya karein?

text.en: Let them rest seated for 5 minutes and repeat the measurement before judging
text.ur: Unhein 5 minute baith kar rest karne dein aur faisla karne se pehle measurement dohrayein

feedback.en: Yes — exercise raises blood pressure temporarily; a fair reading needs a rested patient.
feedback.ur: Haan — exercise blood pressure ko waqti taur par barhati hai; munsifana reading ke liye rested patient chahiye.

feedback.en: A single post-exertion reading cannot diagnose hypertension.
feedback.ur: Exertion ke baad ek reading hypertension ki tashkhees nahi kar sakti.

feedback.en: A high reading still needs a proper repeat.
feedback.ur: Zyada reading ko phir bhi sahi dohrana zaroori hai.

intro.en: Keep your fingers on the wrist **as if still taking the pulse** so the patient does not change their breathing. Watch the chest rise and fall for 30 seconds and double it; note depth, effort and pattern. Normal adult 12–20 breaths per minute; above 20–24 or below 10 is a warning.
intro.ur: Ungliyan wrist par aise rakhein **jaise abhi bhi pulse le rahe hon** taake patient apni saans na badle. Chest ka uthna girna 30 seconds dekhein aur double karein; depth, effort aur pattern note karein. Normal adult 12–20 breaths per minute; 20–24 se upar ya 10 se neeche warning hai.

text.en: **Numbers that change what you do.** A resting heart rate above 100 or below 50 with symptoms, a blood pressure above about 180/110 or below 90 systolic, or a respiratory rate above 24 means: stop, recheck, and tell the nurse or doctor before any exercise. Record every vital with the position and activity ("HR 78 regular, seated, rested") so the trend is meaningful, and use the same arm and the same machine over time.
text.ur: **Woh numbers jo aap ka kaam badal dete hain.** Aaraam mein heart rate 100 se upar ya 50 se neeche symptoms ke saath, blood pressure takriban 180/110 se upar ya systolic 90 se neeche, ya respiratory rate 24 se upar ka matlab hai: ruk jayein, dobara check karein aur kisi bhi exercise se pehle nurse ya doctor ko batayein. Har vital ko position aur activity ke saath likhein (“HR 78 regular, baitha hua, rested”) taake trend mayne rakhe, aur waqt ke saath wohi arm aur wohi machine use karein.

question.en: Why is respiratory rate often called the most neglected vital sign?
question.ur: Respiratory rate ko aksar sab se nazar-andaz ki gayi vital sign kyun kaha jata hai?

answer.en: It is counted by eye, so people estimate or skip it, yet it is among the **best early predictors of deterioration** (cardiac arrest, sepsis, ICU admission). A rate over 24 or a pattern change often appears hours before heart rate or blood pressure changes. Count it for a full 30–60 seconds.
answer.ur: Isay aankh se ginte hain, is liye log andaza lagate hain ya chhor dete hain, halankeh yeh **bigarti halat ke behtareen shuruati predictors** mein se hai (cardiac arrest, sepsis, ICU admission). 24 se upar rate ya pattern ki tabdeeli aksar heart rate ya blood pressure badalne se ghanton pehle nazar aati hai. Poore 30–60 seconds ginein.

question.en: Which pulse finding needs a full 60-second count?
question.ur: Kaun si pulse finding poore 60 second ginti maangti hai?

feedback.en: Yes — an irregular rhythm (for example atrial fibrillation) makes a 30-second count unreliable.
feedback.ur: Haan — irregular rhythm (maslan atrial fibrillation) 30 second ki ginti ko ghair-bharosay ka bana deti hai.

feedback.en: A regular rhythm can be doubled from 30 seconds.
feedback.ur: Regular rhythm 30 seconds se double ki ja sakti hai.

feedback.en: Strength does not change the counting time.
feedback.ur: Strength ginti ka waqt nahi badalti.

text.en: **Stop and call for help** if a patient has a heart rate above 130 or below 40, a systolic pressure below 90 or above 200, chest pain, severe breathlessness, a respiratory rate above 30, confusion or collapse. Do not start exercise; lay the patient down, call a nurse or doctor, and stay with them.
text.ur: **Ruk jayein aur madad bulayein** agar patient ka heart rate 130 se upar ya 40 se neeche, systolic pressure 90 se neeche ya 200 se upar, seene ka dard, shadeed saans ki takleef, respiratory rate 30 se upar, confusion ya behoshi ho. Exercise shuru na karein; patient ko lita dein, nurse ya doctor ko bulayein aur un ke saath rahein.

summary.en: Normal resting adult: pulse 60–100, BP about 120/80, respiratory rate 12–20.
summary.ur: Normal aaraam mein adult: pulse 60–100, BP takriban 120/80, respiratory rate 12–20.

summary.en: Good technique wins: fingertips not thumb, rested and supported patient, right cuff, slow deflation, count respiration without telling the patient.
summary.ur: Acha technique jeetta hai: fingertips thumb nahi, rested aur supported patient, sahi cuff, aahista deflation, patient ko batae bagair respiration ginein.

summary.en: Record numbers with context, repeat odd readings and stop and escalate for abnormal values with symptoms.
summary.ur: Numbers ko context ke saath likhein, ajeeb readings dohrayein aur symptoms ke saath ghair-mamooli values par ruk kar escalate karein.

front.en: Normal adult resting pulse, BP and respiratory rate?
front.ur: Normal adult aaraam ki pulse, BP aur respiratory rate?

back.en: 60–100 bpm, about 120/80 mmHg and 12–20 breaths per minute.
back.ur: 60–100 bpm, takriban 120/80 mmHg aur 12–20 breaths per minute.

front.en: How fast should you deflate the cuff?
front.ur: Cuff kitni tezi se deflate karein?

back.en: 2–3 mmHg per second; first sound is systolic, sounds disappearing is diastolic.
back.ur: 2–3 mmHg per second; pehli awaz systolic, awaz ka ghayab hona diastolic.

front.en: How big should the cuff bladder be?
front.ur: Cuff ka bladder kitna bara ho?

back.en: About 80% of the arm circumference; too small reads falsely high.
back.ur: Arm ki circumference ka takriban 80 %; chhoti cuff jhooti zyada reading deti hai.

front.en: Why count respiration without telling the patient?
front.ur: Patient ko batae bagair respiration kyun ginte hain?

back.en: Awareness changes breathing; keep your fingers on the wrist as if still taking the pulse.
back.ur: Agahi saans ko badal deti hai; ungliyan wrist par aise rakhein jaise pulse le rahe hon.
